mode_evidence: Russell contrasts the ordinary cloudy gloom behind closed lids with a luminous field, says the pictures have motion, light and colour 'perfect as things seen passing before the physical eyes', and spends the Analytic chapters arguing they are seen, not remembered or composed. He also admits some experiences were at the 'inner eyes' in the brain, so the boundary with imaginal seeing is not sharp.
onset_evidence: To the person who sees nothing: sustained meditation and focusing the will 'to a burning-point'. First comes stupor and blankness (seeing, hearing and imagining nothing), which he says clears after weeks or months of persistence, and then the brain grows luminous. He says he knows others with no natural vision who acquired it this way, and that the highest ecstasy is conditioned by law and attainable by all. Prerequisite: unwavering daily concentration and aspiration; no grace or transmission claim in the digest.

conditions.posture: often lying on a hillside or sand dunes; sitting also implied
conditions.setting: alone, outdoors in nature or in quiet meditation
conditions.duration_and_schedule: weeks or months of persistence before the stupor lifts
conditions.prerequisites: intense will and aspiration; he had some natural imagination but says others without it succeeded
conditions.other: visions often arrived in meditation on a theme, or while passive on the earth

stages.label: stupor
stages.description: On reversing habitual outward motions, nothing is seen, heard or imagined; the meditation seems barren.

stages.label: luminous brain
stages.description: After weeks or months the dark caverns of the brain grow luminous; the luminous quality became normal and at times an almost intolerable lustre broke in.

stages.label: visions
stages.description: Shining faces, processions, landscapes, self-shining valleys, light-filled figures; at times a flash of light opens like a gate on a figure.

stages.label: awakened fire
stages.description: At the apex of intense meditation fire ran up the spine, with pulsations as of wings about the head and a cymbal-like sound.

what_to_do_with_light: Let it deepen as meditation proceeds; he cautions against being lured from the highest meditation by the beauty of the forms, and he stayed contemplative rather than drive the awakened fire.
obstacles_and_fixes: Initial stupor and blankness: persist through weeks or months
Being lured by the mirage of forms away from the highest meditation
Recoil into darkness and misery after vision
cautions: Danger of 'misdirection' of the awakened spinal fire; he stayed contemplative in half terror
Meditating on new symbolic associations would encourage madness if they do not become intellectually coherent
Chasing forms tempts one from the highest meditation
interpretation: Russell takes the light to be a self-created luminosity of the subtle aethers transmuted by will and aspiration, a new vesture for the soul that opens onto real planes of the Earth-spirit and the Many-Coloured Land.
practice_summary: Sit or lie alone with the eyes shut and hold the mind on a single chosen object of meditation, aspiring toward the Self, without wavering and as a daily discipline. Expect the first weeks or months to bring only a stupor in which nothing is seen or imagined. Persist. The gloom behind the lids begins to glow, first as a general luminousness and later as bursts of light, figures and landscapes. Do not follow the pretty forms away from the meditation itself. Passive receptivity in quiet places (hillside, shore, pool) also lets coloured scenes appear. If strong fire rises along the spine, do not push it; stay contemplative. Russell says others with no natural vision acquired it by sustained meditation and by focusing the will to a burning-point. The digest does not show the exact object he recommends.
